blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — recognition and escalation of postoperative surgical-site infection
stem: On postoperative day 5, a client has new fever, increasing incisional pain, erythema extending from the wound, and purulent drainage. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Reassure the client that the drainage and worsening pain reflect expected inflammatory healing, then continue routine wound care without additional assessment or escalation.
options.B: Remove the sutures independently before surgical-team evaluation because opening the incision is the nurse's first-line treatment for suspected postoperative infection.
options.C: Begin leftover oral antibiotics brought from home before the wound is evaluated because immediate unsupervised antimicrobial treatment is preferred to diagnostic assessment.
options.D: Perform a focused wound and systemic assessment, notify the surgical team promptly, and obtain ordered diagnostic specimens while following wound and infection-control measures.

rationale: CDC/NHSN 2026 surgical-site infection criteria identify purulent drainage, fever, new or worsening localized pain/tenderness, erythema, and other evidence of infection as concerning postoperative findings. These findings warrant focused assessment and prompt escalation rather than routine reassurance, independent wound opening, or use of unprescribed antibiotics. Therefore D is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize postoperative surgical-site infection findings and perform focused assessment with prompt surgical-team notification and ordered diagnostic evaluation.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN)
source_locator: 2026 SSI checklist: purulent drainage is an SSI criterion; deep-incisional SSI criteria include fever >38°C and new/worsening localized pain or tenderness; superficial SSI criteria include erythema/redness and pain/tenderness when the incision is opened/evaluated.
source_claim_supported: Postoperative purulent drainage with fever, worsening pain, and erythema is concerning for SSI and requires assessment and clinical escalation rather than routine observation.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential: monitor diagnostic findings/trends, recognize complications, perform focused assessments, and intervene as needed.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Removed all-based cueing and rewrote all options as complete management actions of comparable length.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms D uniquely matches 2026 CDC/NHSN SSI criteria and safe nursing escalation; no residual absolute-word cue or second answer remains.
